title: Nine BART employees faced a $15,000 salary gap. What did later job applicants see?

beats.text: One BART employee negotiated higher starting pay. Nine others in the same classification did not.

visual.sub: Nine employees in one classification faced a pay gap

beats.text: The inspector reported a $15,000 annual gap.

visual.label: Nine employees in one classification faced a pay gap

beats.text: It found inconsistent salary decisions. It did not find evidence that discrimination drove them.

visual.kicker: Nine employees in one classification faced a pay gap

beats.text: BART later processed salary adjustments effective May twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-four.

visual.kicker: Salary adjustments and an audit had separate outcomes

beats.text: The district gave no individual amounts.
Human Resources approved a separate federal pay review in December.

visual.kicker: Salary adjustments and an audit had separate outcomes

beats.text: In 2025, the rules changed for new hires in one bargaining unit.
The new agreement permits hiring above step one with approval.

visual.kicker: A later bargaining agreement changed the pay rules prospectively

beats.text: A 2025 vacancy called pay negotiable yet printed only the first step as its opening offer.
Another gave the entire five-step range and called the starting salary negotiable.

visual.kicker: Two hiring bulletins described entry pay differently

beats.text: The job postings show what applicants saw. Individual offers are still needed.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
